name: Frikkadels
summary: Spiced beef meatballs, browned and then simmered in a sweet-sour tomato and onion sauce until tender, for spooning over mash.
about: Frikkadels are a mainstay of Afrikaans home cooking, and Cape kitchens make them too. The mince is bound with soaked bread and egg and seasoned with onion, nutmeg, coriander and a dash of Worcestershire sauce. They are fried or baked, often finished in tomato sauce, and served with mashed potato, rice and peas. Leftovers are eaten cold on bread.
steps: Tear the bread into a large bowl, pour over the milk and leave for 5 minutes until soft, then mash it to a paste with a fork.

Add the mince, grated onion, garlic, egg, parsley, coriander, nutmeg, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper. Mix with your hands for about a minute, just until evenly combined; overworking makes the frikkadels tough.
With wet hands, roll the mixture into about 18 balls the size of a golf ball and flatten them slightly.

Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the frikkadels in two batches, turning them, until crusted and brown all over, 5–6 minutes a batch. Lift them onto a plate; they will finish cooking in the sauce.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of fat. Fry the sliced onion over medium heat until soft and golden, about 6 minutes, then add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, water, sugar, vinegar and bay leaf. Bring to the boil, then simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until slightly thickened. Taste and season with salt.

Return the frikkadels and their juices to the sauce in a single layer. Cover and simmer over low heat for 20 minutes, turning them once, until cooked through with no pink in the middle and the sauce is thick. Serve with mashed potato or rice and peas.
prepNote: Roll the frikkadels in the morning and keep them covered in the fridge; the cooked dish keeps 2 days and reheats well.
